S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

patient_info.stressor: After Ralph Matthews’s divorce, returning to dating and maintaining his visible front-of-house role at the restaurant made him feel as if his appearance was being judged in a way it had not been during the settled years of marriage. He became increasingly preoccupied with a perceived defect in his hairline and facial appearance that guests and coworkers did not seem to notice, and his preparation before shifts expanded into repeated mirror checking, retaking photographs, grooming, and mentally reviewing how he looked under the restaurant lights. The concern grew clinically significant when he began arriving late, declining gallery events and hikes, avoiding staff photographs, and losing confidence in the calm guest-facing role he had built over two decades. Following a serious work warning about missed shifts and disrupted floor coverage, he used the restaurant’s employee assistance referral and was directed to psychiatric care.

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: I’m here because I can’t stop thinking that my hairline and the way my face looks under the restaurant lights make me look old and strange, even when my coworkers tell me they don’t see what I’m talking about.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Before a shift I keep checking the bathroom mirror, taking phone pictures from different angles, combing my hair forward, and replaying how guests might see me until I’m late or too worked up to go out front.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I’ve been written up at the restaurant because I’m late or miss shifts, and I’ve stopped going to staff photos, gallery events, and hikes because I can’t handle being seen that way.
